title: SPUR publishes AI content tracking standard, pitches OpenAI and Google to join advisory board
key_facts: The Standards for Publisher Usage Rights initiative (SPUR) released a content telemetry standard on 2 Oct 2026 for tracking how AI tools use publishers' content.
SPUR, formed in March, includes the Guardian, the Financial Times, the BBC, Sky, The Times of London, MediaHaus and the AP.
The standard sets out a process to track and report when content is retrieved, grounded (used as evidence for an AI answer), cited, presented and engaged with, and to report that back to publishers.
SPUR invited OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and Microsoft to join a new invitation-only AI Licensing Advisory Board of about 20 members, with a first meeting planned for October.
A Google spokesperson said only that it frequently engages with SPUR and other associations; the other companies did not respond before publication.
A draft standard was published in June and open for comment until 24 July; the first version adds support for more than text.
SPUR's first technical committee meets on 15 Oct to decide how the signals sent by AI tools will be checked.
Pilot programs with tech and AI companies come next; SPUR's technical lead declined to name participants.
quote_evidence: A coalition of media organizations, including the Guardian and the Financial Times, has released a new standard for tracking how AI tools use publishers’ content.
When asked whether Google had accepted SPUR’s invitation to join the board, a spokesperson said, “We frequently engage with SPUR and other associations on a variety of topics.”
The other companies did not respond to requests for comment before publishing time.
why_it_matters_hint: If AI companies adopt it, publishers would get consistent data on when their content is used in AI answers, a starting point for licensing talks; none has agreed yet.
event_date: 2 Oct 2026 (standard released 'today' per Digiday, published 2 Oct)
notes: Single outlet. Digiday corrected its headline to say the companies were invited to the advisory board, not to the standard itself; this entry follows the corrected version. Adoption by AI companies is only proposed.
